119832.name: Chabad Ocean Synagogue
119832.note: Lubavitch.com (obituary of Chasiah Kudan): she and Rabbi Dovid Kudan moved to South Broward in 1989 to run youth programs for Chabad of South Broward; 'The next year' they opened the Chabad Ocean Synagogue. Its building campaign page: services first at the Hilton, mostly Holocaust survivors, then Sea Air Towers, then the Hallmark Condominiums; now Chabad Ocean Drive.

118660.name: California Club Chabad
118660.note: Rabbi Shloime and Feigie Halsband's page: 'The California Club Chabad opened its doors in 2003'; it began in a mall and 'after two years we purchased a house to serve as our shul' (825 NE 205 Terrace). (A tribute calls the late Rabbi Dovid Bryn, d. 2002, founder of 'the California Club Shul' too: an earlier minyan there, perhaps.)

160742.name: Chabad of Brandon & South Shore
160742.note: Rabbi Mendel and Tzippy Rubashkin opened Chabad of Brandon 'in the summer of 2004'; a 2005 article: he 'started Chabad of Brandon a year ago' after moving from Brooklyn. Later its Jewish Discovery Center (Valrico, 2014).

169223.name: Chabad at Florida International University
169223.note: Lubavitch.com (via CrownHeights.info, 27 Feb 2007): 'ChabadFIU opened its doors in August of 2004 and quickly outgrew the townhouse they rented just west of the University Park campus'; its own center at 10031 SW 15 Terrace dedicated 11 March 2007 (Rabbi Levi and Sashie Friedman). Now Rabbi Berel and Henny Garelik.

earlier.where: a rented townhouse just west of FIU's University Park campus

169346.name: Chabad of Bradenton & Lakewood Ranch
169346.note: The Observer (Mar 2012): formed in 2004 by Rabbi Mendy and Chanie Bukiet; the Observer, Aug 2009: its fifth year, begun in the Bukiets' East County home, then a nearby school. Bradenton Herald (Mar 2012): 'After meeting more than seven years in living rooms, or in rented space at schools and office buildings', its own home at 5712 Lorraine Road.

earlier.where: Rabbi Mendy and Chanie Bukiet's home, East County
rented space at schools and office buildings

223658.name: Chabad of Cape Coral
223658.note: Established in 2004 by Rabbi Yossi and Rivky Labkowski, 'originally launched in a living room'; later he had lived in Cape Coral for 19 years (Israel National News, 2023).

212291.name: Chabad of Bonita Springs, Estero & FGCU
212291.note: The Banner (via CrownHeights.info, 25 May 2007): building a synagogue 'is a dream for the 3-year-old Chabad of Bonita Springs and Estero' (Rabbi Mendy Greenberg), which had just moved into a 2,000 sq ft office space off Old 41 Road after renting rooms for each event. therebbesimpact.com: 2004.

earlier.where: an office suite in a strip mall off Old 41 Road, Bonita Springs
